key_insight: A density-based topology optimization framework can explicitly account for multidirectional mutual radiation by coupling ray-tracing radiative transfer with finite-element conduction analysis.
engineering_relevance: This enables more physically realistic thermal design of spaceborne heat sinks and radiation shields, where conduction and radiation must be balanced for passive heat rejection.
method: Integrate a zonal-method radiation solver with ray tracing into the thermal FEM loop
Treat intermediate densities as participating media to evaluate radiation on implicit boundaries
Compute design sensitivities analytically with an adjoint method
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation by comparing adjoint sensitivities against finite-difference results and demonstrates optimized heat sink and radiation shield designs.
watch_item: The approach may be computationally expensive because ray tracing and coupled radiation-conduction analysis must be repeated throughout the optimization.
paper_title: Topology optimization of conduction-radiation problems based on a ray-tracing approach
